description: Issue #979: neutralizes the header-value log-leak fix in WTMContext.CallApi.cs's CallAPI<T>. That method loops over the caller-supplied `headers` dictionary and calls client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add(item.Key, item.Value) with NO header-specific catch at all (unlike #961's RestWidgetDataSource/RestEtlSource, which already had a header-specific catch that merely chained the original exception -- here there was nothing to narrow, so the #979 fix ADDS a new try/catch (FormatException) around the Add call, INSIDE the method's existing broad catch (Exception ex), and throws a sanitized InvalidOperationException carrying only the header NAME and the exception TYPE instead of the original exception object). This mutant re-widens that narrow catch back into a leak by replacing the sanitized `throw new InvalidOperationException(...)` with a bare `throw;`, which rethrows the ORIGINAL FormatException unmodified. For a parser-backed header (Authorization is the notable one) .NET's own FormatException.Message embeds the FULL raw attempted header value; that original exception then reaches the method's pre-existing, UNCHANGED broad catch (Exception ex), which hands it whole to WtmDiagnosticLogger.LogError(ex, ...) -- so a logging sink that renders Exception.ToString() (the .NET default) puts the secret back into application logs, reproducing the #979 defect verbatim. red_tests is the log-leak regression test in WtmContextCallApiHeaderLogLeakTests979 (embedded newline in an Authorization header value). green_test is the broad-catch regression test (a completely different code path: an HttpRequestException from the actual HTTP send, no `headers` argument at all) rather than the 'header name still logged' positive control in the same test class -- empirically, the header-name test ALSO fails under this exact mutant (a genuine, verified-by-running-it finding, not assumed): .NET's own FormatException.Message for a rejected Authorization value never mentions the header name at all ('The format of value ... is invalid.'), so the header-name assertion depends on the SAME line this mutant reverts (the synthesized InvalidOperationException's message, which is the only place '{item.Key}' gets embedded) and is not independent of the mutation. Using it as the green_test produced VERDICT: POSITIVE_CONTROL_FAILED, which is a correct verdict, not a bug in the mutant or the test -- it just means that test is the wrong choice of positive control for THIS specific one-line mutant. The broad-catch regression test exercises code the mutant's patch does not touch at all, so it proves what a positive control needs to prove here: the mutation's damage is scoped to the header-rejection path, not the whole method. The sibling defect in src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Services/WtmApiClient.cs (byte-for-byte the same shape, same fix) is deliberately NOT covered by a second mutant entry here -- test/mutants/run_mutant.py's scope check constrains a single patch to a single target_file, and WtmApiClientHeaderLogLeakTests979 already exercises that file's fix directly (its own leak/positive-control/broad-catch tests), so a second mutant would add gate runtime without adding coverage this direct test does not already provide.
target_symbol: WTMContext.CallAPI<T>(...) -- the header-adding loop's inner `catch (FormatException ex)` block's `throw new InvalidOperationException(...)`, line ~68

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Security.WtmCo: to contain "s3cr3t-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me" because the secret must never reach the log

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed:
Captured from an actual `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant 979-callapi-header-exception-leak-reintroduce` run (which builds/tests at -c Release, per #959) against this exact patch/entry pair. A first attempt used a placeholder pattern and correctly produced VERDICT: UNEXPECTED_RED (pattern mismatch only, not a wrong-cause failure) -- following #961's own documented lesson that Python's `.` does not span newlines under re's default flags, this pattern is anchored on the single-line FluentAssertions suffix text rather than trying to span the multi-line exception dump. The real failure message was: Did not expect string "CallAPI failed to 'http://test/api'
System.FormatException: The format of value 'Bearer s3cr3t-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me
X-Injected: evil' is invalid.
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaderParser.ParseValue(...)
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaders.ParseAndAddValue(...)
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaders.Add(...)
   at WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.WTMContext.CallAPI[T](...) in .../WTMContext.CallApi.cs:line 47" to contain "s3cr3t-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me" because the secret must never reach the log, whether via the message template or the logged exception's own text. -- confirming the mutant's bare `throw;` (rethrowing the original FormatException unmodified) is exactly what CapturingLogger's Exception.ToString() rendering picks up, reproducing the pre-fix leak verbatim. After narrowing the pattern to the fixed FluentAssertions suffix text, re-ran to confirm the match. Also discovered (and corrected for) that the originally-chosen green_test_filter ('header name still logged' positive control) fails under this same mutant for a genuine reason -- see the top-level description field for why the broad-catch regression test was substituted instead.
